description: This dataset is the New Jersey Department of Environmental Protection layer of permitted combined sewer overflow outfall points across the state, published on the New Jersey Geographic Information Network hub and as an ArcGIS map service. Combined sewers carry rainwater, domestic sewage and industrial wastewater in one pipe and overflow to a water body when heavy rain or snowmelt exceeds sewer or treatment capacity. Each point carries the NJPDES permit number, the three-digit discharge serial number, coordinates, an alternate name such as a street address, municipality, watershed management area, receiving waterbody, receiving treatment plant and permit, whether the outfall has solids and floatables treatment, and a link to discharge monitoring report data and a website. The state says the data support permitting, planning and public notification under the National CSO Control Policy. Coverage: statewide outfall points, with the item last modified in December 2023. Access: free; distribution is subject to the NJDEP Data Distribution Agreement, which provides the data as is without warranty. Caveats: point locations only, no overflow volumes, and no obligation on the state to update. It supports discharge exposure and combined system performance simulations and relates to the Canadian CSO volume and EPA overflow event records in the catalogue.
